asof: Settles Wed 11 Nov 2026 · written Thu 12 Nov
headline: Holiday futures extend the CPI selloff: reds up 5.5–7.5bp, U7 peak at 4.725% prices more than three hikes.
summary: With cash Treasuries shut for Veterans Day, SR3 kept selling off in the reds: U7 rose 7bp to 4.725%, Z7 7.5bp to 4.69%, M7 5.5bp to 4.695% and H8 7.5bp to 4.645%, while H7 rose only 2.5bp to 4.555%, Z6 1bp to 4.29% and U6 held at 3.925%. Week-to-date M7 and U7 are both 33bp higher and Z6 14.5bp; from the 30 October settle H7–U7 are up 20–21.5bp against 7.5bp in Z9. The peak sits in U7 at 4.725%, 84.5bp over the 3.88% SOFR fixing, with 25.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is more than three hikes, above the Goldman and Macquarie call of December plus March.
drivers: Chicago's Goolsbee called October's 0.4% CPI borderline disturbing, adding to Logan's case for moving faster this winter and Waller's 50bp talk. Treasury futures fell by the equivalent of 2–4bp in yield, and in SR3 the selling concentrated in M7–H8, up 5.5–7.5bp, which pushed H7/M7 to +14bp.
Fed funds futures reprice the whole cycle

Tuesday's post-CPI ZQ snapshot has 28.2bp for 9 December (a 13% chance of 50bp), 44.5bp by January, 62.2bp by March and a 77bp peak by September 2027, up from 20.4bp, 26.5bp, 37.6bp and 50.5bp on Monday. Goldman added a March hike to its forecast for a 4.25–4.5% peak, still below what U7 now implies.

Brent settled $1.27 higher at $92.76 after Iran's security chief said enriched nuclear material would stay in the country, though it is still down about 21% this month. The bounce helped carry the selloff past the peak: H8 and Z7 rose 7.5bp and Z8 6.5bp, against 3.5bp in Z9.
Paulson and a thin holiday session keep the front anchored

Philadelphia's Paulson backed further gradual tightening rather than a faster pace, and with no SOFR fixing or cash trading the front barely moved: Z6 rose 1bp and U6 was unchanged at 3.925%, so U6/Z6 edged up only 1bp to +36.5bp.
spreads: The curve steepened from the front to the reds and inverted further beyond them. U6/Z6 rose 1bp to +36.5bp and Z6/H7 1.5bp to +26.5bp (+14bp each week-to-date), H7/M7 3bp to +14bp (+4.5bp on the week, +1.5bp on the month) and M7/U7 1.5bp to +3bp, while U7/Z7 edged up 0.5bp to −3.5bp, leaving U7 the peak by 3bp over M7 and 3.5bp over Z7. Z6/Z7 widened 6.5bp to +40bp and Z6/M7 4.5bp to +40.5bp (+18.5bp week-to-date, +7bp on the month). Past the peak Z7/H8 held at −4.5bp and H8/M8 slipped to −4bp; Z7/Z8 fell 1bp to −14bp (−10.5bp on the week, −6.5bp on the month), Z8/Z9 3bp to −8bp (−5.5bp on the month) and U7/Z8 0.5bp to −17.5bp (−13bp on the week, −7.5bp on the month), with the 2029 consecutive spreads between −2.5bp and −1bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 1.5bp to +11bp (+2.5bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 1bp to +6.5bp (flat on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Tuesday's after CPI, prices 28.2bp for the 9 December meeting (an 87% chance of 25bp and 13% of 50bp), 44.5bp by January, 62.2bp by March, 75.9bp by June and a 77bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.65%). That compares with 20.4bp, 26.5bp, 37.6bp, 48.4bp and a 50.5bp peak on Monday, 19.7bp, 26.5bp, 40.9bp, 56.1bp and 61bp a week earlier on 3 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 10.6bp on the month and the peak 20bp. Wednesday's SR3 settles run ahead of that snapshot: with SOFR and EFFR both at 3.88%, U7 at 4.725% is 7.5bp over the 4.65% ZQ peak, while Z6 at 4.29% sits between the December (4.16%) and January (4.325%) ZQ rates, in line with a 25bp December hike plus a good chance of another in January. Goldman and Macquarie expect December and March hikes for a 4.25–4.5% peak and Paulson prefers a gradual pace, while Logan wants at least 50bp more; at more than three hikes, the strip is at the hawkish end of that range.

ideas.title: H7/M7 stopped; fade the third hike with a long SR3U7
ideas.why: The short H7/M7 spread hit its +13bp stop as it rose 3bp to +14bp, a 5bp loss from +9bp entry: M7 rose 33bp week-to-date against 28.5bp in H7, so the market extended hikes rather than front-loading them, and we close it. We keep the view that the cycle is overpriced but express it at the peak, where U7 at 4.725% is 84.5bp over SOFR, more than three hikes against the December-plus-March call; 11.5bp to target against 7.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A firm PPI on Friday or strong retail sales on 17 November could push pricing towards a fourth hike and U7 through 4.80%.

ideas.title: Keep the U7/Z8 flattener against a longer cycle
ideas.why: Open and flat at −17.5bp: U7 rose 7bp and Z8 6.5bp, so the oil bounce lifted the 2028 contracts almost as much as the peak. It is now also the offset to the long U7 core, gaining if hot data keeps adding hikes to 2027 while the market still prices 25.5bp of easing from U7 to Z9; 5.5bp to target against 3.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A sharp equity selloff or a soft PPI that brings back haven buying in the reds would lift the spread above −14bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 was unchanged at 3.925% and is up just 0.5bp week-to-date while M7 and U7 rose 33bp, against the 3.88% SOFR fixing for 9 November. Only its last week sees the 9 December decision, so even the 13% chance of 50bp is worth little on the contract, while refunding notes settle on 16 November.
ideas.risk: If refunding settlement tightens funding, SOFR could print back near 3.95% and cost a couple of bp.

watch: Cash Treasuries reopen after the holiday; a third tail after weak 3- and 10-year sales would test the greens and Z8/Z9.
Consensus is 0.4%; a firm pipeline reading would back 50bp in December and test the long U7 core.
